segments.narration: A sheet of paper won't fit between these hundred-ton stones. Sacsayhuamán, above Cusco, at three thousand seven hundred metres.
No mortar. Every block a different shape, and every one meets its neighbours exactly. Three terraced walls, each about four hundred metres long.
The limestone came from quarries kilometres away, over Andean ridges, with no iron tools, no wheels and no draft animals. So how?
Cieza de León wrote in fifteen fifty-three that Pachacuti put twenty thousand men on it, four thousand quarrying, six thousand hauling on leather cables.

Best reconstruction: pounded to shape with hammerstones, hauled on ropes and ramps, test-fitted again and again. And the crooked joints are the point. Inca walls settle back into place when the ground shakes.

verdicts.claim: Sacsayhuamán's largest limestone blocks weigh from about 128 to nearly 200 tonnes and are fitted without mortar so tightly that a coin or paper will not pass between them.

verdicts.claim: Inca blocks show hammerstone impact marks and were fitted by repeated adjustment, and the mortarless inclined masonry gives the walls exceptional seismic resistance.
verdicts.note: Inca architecture article: stones 'initially fit using hammerstones', impact marks visible on many faces, blocks lifted with rope slings and adjusted by eye; inclined walls and rounded corners produced 'peerless seismic resistance', with blocks 'dancing' and resettling in strong earthquakes. Narration says 'best reconstruction' because the exact shaping sequence is inferred, not recorded.

candidates.text: Some stones in this Inca wall weigh over a hundred tons.
candidates.why: A big number, but weight alone is easy to shrug off.

candidates.text: A sheet of paper won't fit between these hundred-ton stones.
candidates.why: Two scales in one image, the tiniest and the heaviest, which is what makes it feel impossible.

candidates.text: Spaniards spent centuries stealing this wall and left the big stones.
candidates.why: Good on the aftermath, but needs the wall introduced first.

choice.reason: The paper-versus-hundred-tonnes contrast is instantly visual with no setup, and it poses the how without answering it.
